data.name: La Bufadora Tour in Baja California
data.headline: Four-hour guided trip from Ensenada to La Bufadora to view the blow hole, browse a handicraft market, and enjoy seaside restaurants.
data.description: This 4-hour guided tour travels from Ensenada to the Punta Banda peninsula to see La Bufadora, North America’s largest sea geyser. Enjoy coastal scenery en route, watch powerful water spouts that can reach more than 100 feet, and learn about the phenomenon from a bilingual guide. After viewing the blow hole, stroll a lively crafts market with time to shop or relax at nearby seaside restaurants. Bottled water and snacks are provided; food and drinks are available for purchase.
data.highlights:
* See La Bufadora, a dramatic sea geyser that can shoot water more than 100 feet into the air.
* Guided coastal drive with commentary and scenic ocean views.
* Time to shop for unique Baja California handicrafts and relax at seaside restaurants.
* Visit the famous Andaluz Bar where the Margarita drink was invented.
data.itinerary:
1. Midmorning pickup in Ensenada and scenic 24-mile (39 km) drive to Punta Banda peninsula.
2. Walk about three blocks through the market with your guide to the La Bufadora blow hole.
3. Observe La Bufadora as waves force water up through the sea cave every 1–2 minutes.
4. Free time to browse the sidewalk crafts market and visit nearby restaurants (own expense).
5. Meet the guide at 1:00 pm to return to hotels by 2:00 pm.

data.faqs:
Where are the designated pickup and drop-off points for this tour?
Complimentary pickup and drop-off are included from any hotel, Airbnb, or vacation
Can I book this tour if I am driving my own car from California, Arizona, or Texas?
Yes. Many visitors drive south via Mexico Federal Highway 1. You can safely park your vehicle at your Ensenada hotel or a secure downtown lot and let our professional drivers handle the road to Punta Banda.
How long is the total travel time during this tour?
The tour has a total duration of 4 hours. The drive from downtown Ensenada to La Bufadora takes approximately 45 minutes each way, giving you plenty of time to enjoy the site and the local market.
What exactly is La Bufadora and what will we see?
La Bufadora is one of the world's largest marine geysers (and the only one in North America). It shoots ocean water up to 100 feet (30 meters) into the air due to breaking waves trapped in an underwater cave.
Are US Dollars accepted at the La Bufadora street market?
Yes. US Dollars (USD) cash is universally accepted by all vendors, restaurants, and artisans. Mexican Pesos (MXN) are fully welcomed
Can I pay for souvenirs, seafood, or drinks with a credit card?
While larger restaurants near the blowhole accept credit/debit cards, most street vendors and souvenir stalls are cash-only. It is highly recommended to bring small-denomination cash bills (USD or MXN).
Are food, drinks, or shopping items included in the tour price?
The tour price covers your private transportation, a bilingual guide, and cold bottled water. Meals, snacks (like local clams or churros), and souvenirs are purchased separately at your own expense.
Is it necessary to alert my bank before traveling to Ensenada?
Yes. If you plan to use your US or Mexican credit/debit cards in Ensenada's restaurants or shops, notify your bank of your travel dates to prevent your cards from being blocked for international fraud prevention.
What should I wear for the La Bufadora tour?
Wear comfortable walking shoes for the paved market path and a light jacket or windbreaker. Depending on the tide and wind, you may get hit by a light, salty ocean mist when standing near the blowhole viewpoint.
Is this tour safe and suitable for young children and elderly family members?
Yes. The tour is completely family-friendly. The walkway leading to the blowhole is paved and secure. However, please note that the path has a moderate incline and can get very crowded on weekends.
Are there any physical or mobility restrictions for this tour?
Wheelchairs and strollers can navigate the main market path to the viewpoint, but some sections have uneven pavement or steps. Please let us know in your booking notes if anyone in your group has limited mobility so we can adapt the logistics.
Can we combine the La Bufadora tour with a quick wine tasting?
Yes. Because this is a private tour experience, the itinerary can be customized. You can coordinate with us ahead of time to add a stop at a local craft brewery or an Ensenada wine tasting room on the way back.
